parsed.rationale: Both `AsyncNotificationMessage` (Shared/Core/Sources/Core/Observation/AsyncMessage.swift:39) and `MainActorNotificationMessage` (Shared/Core/Sources/Core/Observation/MainActorMessage.swift:43) share two identical members — `makeNotification:(_ message: Self, object: Subject?) -> Notification` and `name:Notification.Name` — and differ only in the `makeMessage` signature: the async variant uses `sending Notification` while the main-actor variant uses plain `Notification`. Extracting the shared contract into a base protocol `NotificationMessage` (in the same Core package) eliminates the duplication and makes the concurrency-specific distinction explicit at the child-protocol level. Both protocols are production code (all context flags false) in the same package, so no cross-package dependency changes are required. A default implementation of `makeNotification` could also be provided via a protocol extension on `NotificationMessage` if the body is identical across conformers.

moved_members: makeNotification:(_ message: Self, object: Subject?) -> Notification
